title: What was promised, what was claimed and what PepsiCo reported
lede: There is no sales line for Crystal Pepsi in any PepsiCo filing. What exists is a projection from Pepsi, a share figure from a trade publisher, estimates of the advertising budget, and three years of careful sentences in the annual report. This section keeps them apart.

blocks.title: Four figures, four different kinds of source

items.text: **Pepsi’s projection** in December 1992: more than 2% of a $47 billion market in the first national year.[^8]
**A trade publisher’s figure** in March 1993: the retail value of the one share point he credited to the brand.[^15] Unverified as a sales total.
**A press estimate** of the launch advertising support.[^8][^19] PepsiCo did not disclose a budget.
**Sales figures published by PepsiCo** for the brand, in dollars or cases, in the 1992, 1993 or 1994 annual reports.[^1][^2][^3]

blocks.title: One year from launch to rework
blocks.subtitle: Crystal Pepsi’s US market share as an index, national launch = 100. The two middle points are from a later newspaper summary, not from PepsiCo.

points.title: test markets only
points.text: On sale in Providence, Dallas and Colorado. No national share; plotted as zero.[^5]

points.title: national launch
points.text: Introduced nationally with a projection of more than 2% of the market.[^8]

points.title: down a quarter
points.text: Share had fallen 25% from its debut, according to a 2016 summary of 1993 reporting.[^31] PepsiCo says the brand helped the first quarter.[^2]

points.title: down by more than half
points.text: The same summary says more than 50% by year-end; plotted as 50.[^31] PepsiCo reports “softening trends.”[^2]

points.title: withdrawn
points.text: The original is replaced by a citrus cola called Crystal. Plotted as zero.[^19]

blocks.source: Index derived from the Carroll County Times / Baltimore Sun, Aug 13, 2016[^31], which summarizes a June 1993 Scripps article we could not open, so the middle points are secondary and unverified. End points are plotting conventions. PepsiCo published no share data.[^2]

blocks.title: A small brand inside a large business
blocks.subtitle: PepsiCo’s domestic beverage sales, and the growth in domestic case sales that the company attributed in part to Crystal Pepsi in 1992 and 1993.
blocks.source: PepsiCo annual reports for 1992, 1993 and 1994.[^1][^2][^3] In 1992 case sales rose 1%, “driven by gains in the Mountain Dew brands and the new brand Crystal Pepsi” and Lipton tea. In 1993 they rose 3%, and “case sales of the Crystal Pepsi brands offset a decline in brands Pepsi and Diet Pepsi.” In 1994 they rose 6% despite “significant declines in the Crystal Pepsi brands.” Case sales growth for 1991 is not in the reports we read.

blocks.title: What PepsiCo told its shareholders
blocks.subtitle: Every substantive mention of the brand in three annual reports.
columns: What it says about Crystal Pepsi
rows: “We introduced brand Crystal Pepsi, a unique-tasting clear cola with 100% natural flavors, no caffeine and no preservatives.” Named one of the best new products of 1992 by Time.[^1]

Case sales “offset a decline in brands Pepsi and Diet Pepsi.” The products “particularly aided first quarter results, but did not significantly impact full year profits.” Because of “softening trends,” the product “is being refined and will be reintroduced in 1994 in a nondiet version only.”[^2]
Growth was “partially offset by significant declines in the Crystal Pepsi brands.”[^3][^4]

blocks.body: The 1992 and 1993 reports are quoted from scans whose text layer has recognition errors; obvious errors are corrected in the quotations. Sales in dollars or cases, advertising actually spent and any write-off are unknown: PepsiCo did not publish them.
